The '''2022–23 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team''' represented the [[University of Kentucky]] in the [[2022–23 NCAA Division I men's basketball season]]. The Wildcats, founding members of the [[Southeastern Conference]], played their home games at [[Rupp Arena]] and were led by [[John Calipari]] in his 14th season as head coach. They finished the season 21–10, 12–6 in SEC play to finish in third place. As the No. 3 seed in the [[2023 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], they were upset in the quarterfinal round by [[2022–23 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|Vanderbilt]]. They received an at-large bid to the [[2023 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]], where they defeated [[2022–23 Providence Friars men's basketball team|Providence]] in the first round before falling to [[2022–23 Kansas State Wildcats men's basketball team|Kansas State]] in the second round to finish the season with a final record of 22–12.

==Previous season==
The [[2021–22 Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball team|Wildcats]] finished the [[2021–22 NCAA Division I men's basketball season|2021–22 season]] 26–8, 14–4 in [[2021–22 Southeastern Conference men's basketball season|SEC play]] to finish a tie for second place. As the No. 3 seed in the [[2022 SEC men's basketball tournament|SEC tournament]], they defeated [[2021–22 Vanderbilt Commodores men's basketball team|Vanderbilt]] in the quarterfinals before losing to [[2021–22 Tennessee Volunteers basketball team|Tennessee]] in the semifinals. They received an at large bid to the [[2022 NCAA Division I men's basketball tournament|NCAA tournament]] as the No. 2 seed in the East region. The Wildcats became just the 10th #2 seed to lose in the First Round of the NCAA Tournament, losing to No. 15-seeded [[2021–22 Saint Peter's Peacocks basketball team|Saint Peter's]] 85–79 in overtime. It also marked the first time Kentucky had suffered a First Round exit under Calipari.

===Class of 2023 commitments===
On November 20, 2021, [[Reed Sheppard]] verbally committed to UK over multiple offers, with [[Louisville Cardinals men's basketball|Louisville]] and [[Virginia Cavaliers men's basketball|Virginia]] among the most active in attempting to recruit him. The son of former UK basketball players [[Jeff Sheppard]] and the former Stacey Reed, he was the first commitment to the 2023 recruiting class.
